To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a soluble sperm factor triggers calcium oscillations and resumption of meiosis in unfertilized eggs of the marine worm C. lacteus.

(i) a soluble sperm factor triggers Ca2+ oscillations and maturing events in unfertilized eggs, (ii) the sperm factor is a protein, and (iii) the sperm factor acts within the ooplsm, not on the egg's surface.

(i) a soluble sperm factor triggers repetitive Ca2+ oscillations and meiosis resumption in oocytes of a worm and (ii) the sperm factor is a protein that is >10 kDa and that requires boiling to be fully effective.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of a soluble factor in sperm that is able to trigger calcium transients in unfertilized eggs.
the identification and characterization of a soluble sperm protein that triggers calcium oscillations and egg maturation.
identifying the molecular basis of sperm-egg recognition in C. lacteus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the sperm of the nemertean C. lacteus possesses a sperm factor that can act as a soluble, intracellular trigger of fertilization-like calcium transients and ooplasmic maturation in the absence of any sperm-egg membrane contact.
the sperm of this marine nemertean possess a soluble proteinaceous factor that can trigger calcium oscillations in the absence of egg surface binding.
the sperm of the marine worm C. lacteus possesses a soluble protein factor that can trigger calcium oscillations, meiotic maturation, and development in unfertilized, oocyte-like cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the sperm of the marine worm C. lacteus contain a sperm-specific protein that can act intracellularly to trigger calcium oscillations, meiotic maturation, and the formation of pronuclei in the absence of any sperm-egg binding.
a soluble sperm factor is capable of triggering Ca2+ oscillations and maturing unfertilized oocyte in the absence of any sperm-egg binding.

a sperm extract, containing a soluble, heat-sensitive, 10-kDa or smaller protein(s), can act within the cytoplasm to trigger calcium oscillations, meiotic maturation, and the formation of the female pronucleus in unfertilized eggs of the marine nemertean C. lacteus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sperm factor can be extracted from a single sperm and that it is sufficient for egg activation in a dose-dependent manner, suggesting that it may have a biological role in natural fertilization.
a soluble sperm factor, in addition to a membrane-bound sperm factor, may be involved in the generation of fertilization-like Ca2+ oscillations in marine worm eggs.
sperm can release soluble proteins that can trigger a fertilization-like response in eggs.
